source_text: Λέγει γὰρ πάλιν περὶ τῶν ὠτίων, πῶς περιέτεμεν ἡμῶν τὴν καρδίαν. λέγει κύριος ἐν τῷ προφήτῃ: Εἰς ἀκοὴν ὠτίου ὑπήκουσάν μου. καὶ πάλιν λέγει: Ἀκοῇ ἀκούσονται οἱ πόρρωθεν, ἃ ἐποίησα γνώσονται. καί: Περιτμήθητε, λέγει κύριος, τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν. καὶ πάλιν λέγει Ἄκουε Ἰσραήλ. ὅτι τάδε λέγει κύριος ὁ θεός σου. καὶ πάλιν τὸ πνεῦμα κυρίου προφητεύει: Τίς ἐστιν ὁ θέλων ζῆσαι εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα; ἀκοῇ ἀκουσάτω τῆς φωνῆς τοῦ παιδός μου. καὶ πάλιν λέγει: Ἄκουε οὐρανέ, καὶ ἐνωτίζου γῆ, ὅτι κύριος ἐλάλησεν ταῦτα εἰς μαρτύριον. καὶ πάλιν λέγει: Ἀκούσατε λόγον κυρίου, ἄρχοντες τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου. καὶ πάλιν λέγει: Ἀκούσατε, τέκνα, φωνῆς βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ. οὐκοῦν περιέτεμεν ἡμῶν τὰς ἀκοάς, ἵνα ἀκούσαντες λόγον πιστεύσωμεν ἡμεῖς. ἀλλὰ καὶ ἡ περιτομή, ἐφ̓ ᾗ πεποίθασιν, κατήργηται, περιτομὴν γὰρ εἴρηκεν οὐ σαρκὸς γενηθῆναι: ἀλλὰ παρέβησαν, ὅτι ἄγγελος πονηρὸς ἐσόφιζεν αὐτούς. λέγει πρὸς αὐτούς: Τάδε λέγει κύριος ὁ θεὸς ὑμῶν ʽὧδε εὑρίσκω ἐντολήν̓: Μὴ σπείρητε ἐπ’ ἀκάνθαις, περιτμήθητε τῷ κυρίῳ ὑμῶν. καὶ τί λέγει; Περιτμήθητε τὴν σκληροκαρδίαν ὑμῶν, καὶ τὸν τράχηλον ὑμῶν οὐ σκληρυνεῖτε. λάβε πάλιν: Ἰδού, λέγει κύριος, πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ἀπερίτμητα ἀκροβυστίαν, ὁ δὲ λαὸς οὗτος ἀπερίτμητος καρδίας. ἀλλ’ ἐρεῖς: Καὶ μὴν περιτέτμηται ὁ λαὸς εἰς σφραγῖδα. ἀλλὰ καὶ πᾶς Σύρος καὶ Ἄραψ καὶ πάντες οἱ ἱερεῖς τῶν εἰδώλων. ἄρα οὖν κἀκεῖνοι ἐκ τῆς διαθήκης αὐτῶν εἰσίν; ἀλλὰ καὶ οἱ Αἰγύπτιοι ἐν περιτομῇ εἰσίν. μάθετε οὖν, τέκνα ἀγάπης, περὶ πάντων πλουσίως, ὅτι Ἀβραάμ, πρῶτος περιτομὴν δούς, ἐν πνεύματι προβλέψας εἰς τὸν Ἰησοῦν περιέτεμεν, λαβὼν τριῶν γραμμάτων δόγματα. λέγει γάρ: Καὶ περιέτεμεν Ἀβραὰμ ἐκ τοῦ οἴκου αὐτοῦ ἄνδρας δεκαοκτὼ καὶ τριακοσίους. τίς οὖν ἧ δοθεῖσα αὐτῷ γνῶσις; μάθετε, ὅτι τοὺς δεκαοκτὼ πρώτους, καὶ διάστημα ποιήσας λέγει τριακοσίους. τὸ δεκαοκτὼ ι δέκα, η ὀκτώ: ἔχεις Ἰησοῦν. ὅτι δὲ ὁ σταυρὸς ἐν τῷ ταῦ ἤμελλεν ἔχειν τὴν χάριν, λέγει καὶ τοὺς τριακοσίους. δηλοῖ οὖν τὸν μὲν Ἰησοῦν ἐν τοῖς δυσὶν γράμμασιν, καὶ ἐν τῷ ἑνὶ τὸν σταυρόν. οἶδεν ὁ τὴν ἔμφυτον δωρεὰν τῆς διδαχῆς αὐτοῦ θέμενος ἐν ἡμῖν. οὐδεὶς γνησιώτερον ἔμαθεν ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ λόγον: ἀλλὰ οἶδα, ὅτι ἄξιοί ἐστε ὑμεῖς.
pass_a_gloss: For he says again concerning the ears, how he circumcised our heart. The Lord says in the prophet: They obeyed me with the hearing of the ear. And again he says: Those far off will hear and know what I have done. And: Be circumcised, the Lord says, your hearts. And again he says: Hear, Israel, for thus says the Lord your God. And again the Spirit of the Lord prophesies: Who is it that wants to live forever? Let him hear the voice of my servant. And again he says: Hear, heaven, and give ear, earth, for the Lord has spoken these things as a testimony. And again he says: Hear the word of the Lord, rulers of this people. And again he says: Hear, children, the voice of one crying in the wilderness. Therefore, he circumcised our ears so that we, having heard the word, might believe. But also the circumcision, in which they have put their trust, has been abolished, for he said that circumcision is not to be of the flesh, but they transgressed because an evil angel was deceiving them. He says to them: Thus says the Lord your God: I find a command here, do not sow among thorns, be circumcised to your Lord. And what does he say? Be circumcised of your hard heart, and do not harden your neck. Take it again: Behold, the Lord says, all the nations are uncircumcised in uncircumcision, but this people is uncircumcised in heart. But you will say: And yet the people is circumcised as a seal. But also every Syrian and Arab and all the priests of the idols are circumcised. Are they then also from their covenant? But also the Egyptians are in circumcision. Learn therefore, children of love, about all things abundantly, that Abraham, first giving circumcision, having foreseen in spirit to Jesus, circumcised, having taken the dogma of three letters. For he says: And Abraham circumcised eighteen and three hundred men from his house. What knowledge was given to him then? Learn that the eighteen first, and having made a space, he says three hundred. The eighteen is ten and eight: you have Jesus. And because the cross was to have the grace in the tau, he says also the three hundred. He indicates then Jesus in the two letters, and in the one the cross. He knows the one who has placed the innate gift of his teaching in us. No one has learned a more genuine word from me, but I know that you are worthy.
pass_b_english: The author returns once more to the theme of the ears, explaining how our hearts were circumcised. The Lord declares through the prophet: 'They obeyed me when they heard with their ears.' And again he says: 'Those far away will hear and come to know what I have done.' Then: 'Circumcise your hearts,' says the Lord. Once more he commands: 'Hear, Israel, for this is what the Lord your God says.' The Spirit of the Lord also prophesies: 'Who wants to live forever? Let that one listen to the voice of my servant.' And again: 'Hear, heavens, and give ear, earth, for the Lord has spoken these things as a testimony.' He says yet again: 'Hear the word of the Lord, you rulers of this people.' And again: 'Listen, children, to the voice of one crying in the wilderness.' Because of this, he has circumcised our ears so that, having heard the word, we might believe.

But the circumcision in which they trust has been abolished, for he declared that circumcision is not to be of the flesh; yet they transgressed because an evil angel deceived them. He speaks to them: 'Thus says the Lord your God: Here I find a command: Do not sow among thorns; circumcise yourselves to the Lord.' (Jeremiah 4:4). And what does he say? 'Circumcise your hard heart, and do not stiffen your neck.' (Deuteronomy 10:16). Consider this again: 'Behold, the Lord says, all the nations are uncircumcised in their uncircumcision, but this people is uncircumcised in heart.' Someone might object: 'Yet the people are circumcised as a seal.' But every Syrian and Arab and all the priests of the idols are circumcised as well. Are they then also part of the covenant? The Egyptians, too, practice circumcision. Therefore, learn abundantly about all things, beloved children, that Abraham, the first to institute circumcision, foresaw Jesus in the Spirit and circumcised, having grasped the teaching of three letters.

For it says: 'Abraham circumcised eighteen and three hundred men from his household.' What knowledge was given to him? Understand this: the eighteen comes first, then a gap, then three hundred. Eighteen is ten plus eight — you have Jesus. And because the cross was to hold the grace in the letter tau, he also gives the three hundred. So he signifies Jesus in the two letters, and the cross in the one. The one who placed the innate gift of his teaching within us knows this. No one has learned a more genuine word from me, but I know that you are worthy.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex numerological and Christological arguments in the Greek text. Pass A provides a literal translation, while Pass B provides a fluent rendering that correctly identifies the scriptural allusions (Jeremiah 4:4 and Deuteronomy 10:16) without misrepresenting the Greek. The interpretation of the 'three letters' (the eighteen/ten and eight for Jesus, and the three hundred for the cross/tau) is faithfully rendered.
